programs.title: Agents at Work, Humans in Charge: A Members' Introduction to Agent-Managed Governance
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate; people govern' model and the six human-reserved actions
Read a DAO charter and identify measurable outcomes and accountability paths
Practice collective decision-making on agent-drafted proposals
Assess how automation could affect members' roles and representation

sessions.activity: Guided reading of the DAO charter and contribution model; members map reserved human powers (final vote, charter amend, treasury transfer) onto union equivalents like ratification votes.
Members review a sample evidence summary from the Evidence Monitor and practice asking critical questions about sources, bias and gaps.
Mock decision cycle: an agent-drafted proposal is debated, amended and voted on by members only, mirroring the human-reserved final vote.
Members interpret progress dashboards and draft member-facing questions for the next steward cycle.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised post-session quiz scores and anonymised poll results on trust in agent-assisted governance, contributed as a labeled civic-education dataset.
programs.consent: Opt-in only; individual responses pseudonymised before aggregation; any sharing beyond the program requires a member vote consistent with the union's own decision rules.

programs.title: Shaking Palsy to Shared Decisions: James Parkinson's Shoreditch and Governing Technology
outcomes: Connect local history (St Leonard's Church, 1817 essay) to the history of medicine and observation
Describe how an agent-managed DAO separates agent work from human votes
Draft and debate a simple proposal as a class decision cycle
Understand basic data privacy and consent in shared projects

sessions.activity: Learners examine how the Evidence Monitor summarizes research; they compare a summary to its source and flag what is missing.
Using James Parkinson's observational method, learners write a mini-charter for a class project with two measurable outcomes.
Class debate and vote on an agent-drafted mock proposal; only students cast the final vote, mirroring human-only governance.
Learners build a simple progress chart for their mini-charter outcomes and present it at St Leonard's / Shoreditch local history framing.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised (no names, no ages beyond grade band) examples of learner-drafted charters and vote tallies, shared as an open civics-education resource.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent required for all data contributions; learners give age-appropriate assent; no individual is identifiable; any withdrawal removes that learner's contributions.

programs.title: Evidence-to-Action: Running Human-Governed Decision Cycles with Agent Support
programs.grade_or_level: Professional development, NGO program and policy staff
outcomes: Design a decision cycle where agents draft and synthesize but humans decide
Translate field evidence into measurable charter outcomes
Map collaborators and working groups using agent-scouted inputs

sessions.activity: Staff workshop: turn a real program question into research questions; critique agent-generated evidence summaries for coverage and bias.
Using the Collaborator Scout and Task Router model, staff map partners and working groups for their own program area around the Shoreditch anchor place.
Staff draft a proposal via a Proposal & Grant Drafter simulation, then run a human-only review and final vote.
Staff define indicators and a tracking cadence for their proposal's outcomes, aligned to the charter's measurable outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised program indicators and lessons-learned notes on agent-assisted decision cycles, contributed to a shared NGO practice library.
programs.consent: Organizational consent via MOU; community-level data aggregated and de-identified; no beneficiary-identifiable data leaves partner organizations.

programs.title: Charter First: Building Measurable Missions for Small Nonprofits
outcomes: Write a one-page charter with 2-3 measurable outcomes
Understand the six human-reserved governance actions and why they stay with people
Set up a simple progress tracking routine
Collect and share data responsibly with tiny teams

sessions.activity: Hands-on clinic: each nonprofit drafts a mini-charter modeled on the DAO's charter structure, with contribution model and outcomes.
Volunteers role-play a decision cycle: agent-drafted proposals are debated and decided by the human board, never auto-enacted.
Teams set up lightweight task routing and working groups using the Task Router pattern adapted to volunteer staffing.
Teams build a one-page progress dashboard and schedule quarterly reviews against their charter outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised charter templates and aggregated outcome-metric patterns, contributed to a shared small-nonprofit toolkit.
programs.consent: Opt-in contribution; organization names and client data stripped before sharing; each team approves exactly what enters the shared toolkit.
